hero.title: UI/UX design services and software development for new and established products
lede: Design and engineering are for the places your product is judged: the people who use it all day, the sales demo, the sprint where engineers build it and the renewal.
Tcules offers UI/UX design services and software development for complex software, with a particular focus on SaaS, from a founder's first idea to products customers have used for years.
Product Design leads every project. We join at the idea stage, inside your product team, or the day a working prototype has to become software customers rely on.

sections.heading: Selected design and development work
sections.intro: Three products, each drawing on a different mix of our services.

cases.heading: ConnectX: an AI energy product taken from definition to a live module
cases.body:
We defined this building-energy product around eight scenarios drawn from the questions its users ask, then proved it in a coded demo on sample data. We then carried the demo into a production-ready module that went live in late 2025.

[Read the ConnectX case](/case-studies/ai-native-building-energy-product-connectx)

media.altIntent: Coded ConnectX workspace demonstrating an AI-assisted building-energy scenario

cases.heading: Eden AI: one search box, with AI help kept separate
cases.body:
Developers on Eden AI's platform can begin a workflow three ways: from a template, from scratch or with the AI's help. Our redesign brought all three into one search box, made AI help a mode you enter on purpose, and gave Eden's own developers specs to build from.

[Read the Eden AI case](/case-studies/eden-ai-workflow-builder-search-redesign)

media.altIntent: Eden AI workflow builder showing unified search and AI-assisted creation

cases.heading: Gold Image Printing: a print store and its production system redesigned together
cases.body:
We watched production staff use the existing system, then redesigned the web-to-print store and the internal ERP on a single component set and style guide. The design gives each order one shape from checkout through artwork, scheduling and fulfilment, and we worked with the client's technical team on implementation.

[Read the Gold Image Printing case](/case-studies/gold-image-printing-web-to-print-erp-modernisation)

sections.heading: How we work together
sections.intro: When you are not sure which service fits, a good first piece of work is one workflow, one feature or a focused audit, run as a small pilot project.

reasons.evidence: Before we shaped [Auxentios'](/case-studies/auxentios-cpq-product-mvp-design) quoting MVP, eight interviews mapped what each of six specialist roles adds to a quotation, and the product structure followed that map.

For [The Wandering Raven](/case-studies/wandering-raven-edtech-moodle-experience), we designed a creative-writing world for young learners, then set up its Moodle plugins and custom theme ourselves, so the design holds together where learners use it.
Primelis brought us in three years ago and has kept us on as an ongoing partnership; we have designed every one of its products since.

sections.heading: Questions about choosing UI/UX design and development services

items.question: Do we need to know which service we want?
items.answer: No. Tcules recommends the service, or mix of services, once you describe the product, where it is heading and what is hard. A few lines will do, and you don't need our service names.

items.question: Can you take a new SaaS product from idea to launch?
items.answer: Yes. Our end-to-end product development services take new SaaS products from first definition to a launch-ready first release, as [New Product Design & First Release](/services/new-product-design-first-release) explains. Already have a working prototype? A [Prototype Readiness Review](/audits/prototype-readiness-review) shows what it needs before customers arrive.

items.question: Can we start with an audit or one workflow?
items.answer: Yes. Tcules treats one workflow, a feature or a focused audit as a strong first step. It runs as a pilot project, so you see how we think about your product before planning anything bigger. [How pilots work](/how-we-work#engagement-shapes)

items.question: What is the difference between Product Design and Design Engineering?
items.answer: Product Design works out what the product does and how it works, through research, workflows and interface design. Design Engineering takes that work into code, so a risky interaction can be tried in a running product and the production interface keeps to the design. The two often run side by side on one project.

items.question: Design Systems or Product Modernisation: which do we need?
items.answer: Choose Design Systems when the trouble is inconsistency: the same button built five ways, or Figma and code drifting apart. Choose Product Modernisation when workflows and technology have aged and need changing in stages. A modernisation can start from a shared component layer, as Benchmark Gensuite's did.

items.question: Should we hire one studio for design and development, or two suppliers?
items.answer:
Separate suppliers suit a finished design that only needs building, but gaps can open before release. Our design with your engineers suits a strong in-house team, as long as someone answers the product questions that land on engineers mid-build; at [Dealpath](/case-studies/enterprise-workflow-redesign-dealpath-real-estate), its own team owned implementation.

One studio suits new products and designs still moving once code starts, with the code we touch agreed early.

items.question: How much do UI/UX design and development services cost?
items.answer: The cost depends on what is designed and built, and how much of it. Each engagement gets its price before any work begins, based on the scope you agree with us. [How pricing works](/how-we-work#engagement-shapes)
